name: George C. Wallace Alabama Supercomputer Center

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 84 (Alabama Supercomputer Authority missing-address campaign): the prior remediation pass reading already named this facilitys address in prose but had not set the structured address field. This session added it, 686 Discovery Drive, Huntsville, AL 35806, confirmed by convergence of ASAs own about page and a maximum confidence reverse geocode of this rows own coordinates, and offered a plausible explanation, Madison County versus the city of Madison, for the earlier notes conflicting aggregator location claim.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This is the Alabama Supercomputer Authority (ASA) data center at 686 Discovery Drive in Cummings Research Park, Huntsville, Alabama. Per ASAs own about page, the Authority was established by the Alabama Legislature in 1989, with a stated mission to provide information technology resources and services for the advancement of education, research, and economic development in Alabama. ASA operates the Alabama Supercomputer Center and oversees the Alabama Research and Education Network (AREN), serving K-12 schools, community colleges, universities, libraries, and government agencies statewide, and per ASAs own homepage has served as the AREN Consortium lead in the federal E-Rate program since 1998. The Authority installed its current ASA-X Supercomputer system in 2023.

The Authority is led by CEO Debra Wallace, named to the role January 1, 2021 after joining ASA in 2008. Per ASAs own news archive (asc.edu/asainthenews), she is the Authoritys first female CEO and its first CEO promoted from within, and brings more than 30 years of experience in accounting, technical administration, and education.

In January 2023, StateScoop reported that General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT) won a five year, 152 million dollar contract, with two option years, covering cybersecurity, software development, high performance computing support, enterprise network management, application development, hybrid multi cloud hosting, IT systems support, and broadband connectivity for ASA, building on an existing 30 year partnership between GDIT and the Authority. CEO Wallace was quoted in that reporting describing the contract as supporting broadband connectivity and related services to more than 780 educational clients statewide, and GDIT vice president Scott Mack was quoted describing it as enhancing ASAs ability to provide fast, secure, and reliable access to research and education resources across Alabama.

No published capacity or megawattage figure was found on ASAs own site. A third party data center aggregator site was found citing a 96.4 megawatt figure and a Madison, Alabama location for this facility, but that source sits at the bottom tier of this registrys source hierarchy, is not corroborated by ASAs own site or by any regulatory filing, and conflicts with the Huntsville, Cummings Research Park address confirmed by ASAs own site, so it is recorded here as an unverified lead rather than adopted as fact.

This session confirmed the specific street address structurally. ASAs own about page gives 686 Discovery Drive, Huntsville, AL 35806 for the Supercomputer Data Center specifically (distinct from a separate Montgomery, AL business office address also listed there), and reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service independently returned an exact match at the services maximum confidence level for the same address, 686 Discovery Drive Northwest, Huntsville, AL 35806. That reverse geocode also returned Madison County as this locations county, which likely explains the earlier notes conflicting third party aggregator claim of a Madison, Alabama location, this facility sits in Madison County but within the city of Huntsville, not the separate city of Madison, Alabama, a plausible source of the aggregators confusion rather than necessarily an error about a different building entirely. The 96.4 megawatt aggregator figure remains unverified and is not adopted.

reading.body:
The George C. Wallace Alabama Supercomputer Center sits in Huntsville's Cummings Research Park with no published capacity figure. A third party aggregator claims 96.4 megawatts, but this figure is unverified, unconfirmed by the Alabama Supercomputer Authority's own site or any regulatory filing, and ranked at the bottom tier of source reliability, so it cannot be treated as fact. The facility's actual IT load remains unknown from published sources.

The Authority installed its current ASA-X Supercomputer in 2023 and operates the Alabama Research and Education Network serving K-12 schools, community colleges, universities, libraries, and government agencies across the state. In January 2023, General Dynamics Information Technology won a five year, 152 million dollar contract to provide cybersecurity, software development, high performance computing support, enterprise network management, and broadband connectivity to more than 780 educational clients statewide. The Authority does not publish whether this facility hosts training accelerators, inference capacity, or serves external AI workloads rather than state research and education alone.

Alabama has 12 mapped data center facilities of which only two publish capacity figures totaling 9.5 megawatts. This campus is ranked third in the state by published megawattage, but that ranking describes only the two published figures above it, not the actual distribution of capacity. Without verified specifications, the campus cannot be placed in regional or national AI infrastructure scaling.
